proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \((i,t)\in G\times W\), suppress the superscript \(it\), and write \(\mathcal O=\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}\), \(Y=R_{it}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and \(\widetilde M=\widetilde M^{it}\).  The local objective in Definition \(\mathrm{def:native\mbox{-}estimator}\) is the proper convex function
\[
 f(A)=\frac12\lVert P_{\mathcal O}(Y-A)\rVert_F^2+\lambda\lVert A\rVert_*.
\]
Because the space is finite dimensional and \(\lambda>0\) by \(\mathrm{ass:penalty\mbox{-}level}\), the convex first-order condition at every minimizer is
\[
 0\in P_{\mathcal O}(\widetilde M-Y)+\lambda\,\partial\lVert\widetilde M\rVert_*.
\]
Set \(Z=P_{\mathcal O}Y+P_{\mathcal O^c}\widetilde M\).  Orthogonality of the two coordinate projections gives
\[
 \widetilde M-Z=P_{\mathcal O}(\widetilde M-Y),
\]
so the preceding condition is exactly
\[
 0\in \widetilde M-Z+\lambda\,\partial\lVert\widetilde M\rVert_*.
\]
This is the necessary and sufficient optimality condition for the strictly convex proximal problem
\[
 \min_A\left\{\frac12\lVert Z-A\rVert_F^2+\lambda\lVert A\rVert_*\right\}.
\]
For completeness, if \(Z=P\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_k)Q^{\top}\) is a singular-value decomposition, von Neumann's trace inequality reduces this problem to the separate scalar minimizations
\[
 \min_{a_k\ge0}\left\{\frac12(\sigma_k-a_k)^2+\lambda a_k\right\},
 \qquad a_k=(\sigma_k-\lambda)_+.
\]
Equality in the trace inequality is obtained by retaining the singular vectors \(P,Q\).  Hence the unique proximal minimizer is \(\operatorname{SVT}_{\lambda}(Z)\), and therefore
\[
 \widetilde M^{it}=\operatorname{SVT}_{\lambda}\!\left(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}+P_{(\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it})^c}\widetilde M^{it}\right).
\]
The argument applies to each minimizer selected by the fixed measurable rule and uses the actual masked objective.

Fix a target \((i,t)\), and write \(E_{it}=E^{it}_{it}\) for its local coordinate matrix.  Let \(P_X\) and \(P_F\) denote the orthogonal projectors onto the column spaces of the local factor matrices \(X_{I_{it}}\) and \(F_{J_{it}}\).  Exact rank and positivity of the local signal give a positive gap between its \(r\)-th and \((r+1)\)-st singular values.  Hence the best rank-\(r\) projection is differentiable at \(M^{it}\).  Its derivative is the orthogonal projection onto the rank-\(r\) tangent space:
\[
 D\mathcal P_r(M^{it})[E]
 =P_XE+EP_F-P_XEP_F.
\]
Indeed, a differentiable rank-\(r\) local chart shows that the derivative belongs to the tangent space, while differentiating the least-squares normal equation makes the residual \(E-D\mathcal P_r(M^{it})[E]\) orthogonal to that space; the displayed expression is exactly this orthogonal projector.  This argument depends only on the two factor spans and therefore remains valid when positive singular values are repeated.

The local completion map fills the missing coordinate by the rank-projection fixed point.  If \(e\) is an observed perturbation, so its target coordinate is set to zero, and \(\delta\) is the derivative of the filled target cell, differentiation of that fixed point gives
\[
 \delta=\left[D\mathcal P_r(M^{it})[e+\delta E_{it}]\right]_{it}.
\]
Set \(P_{jk}=(P_X)_{jk}\), \(Q_{su}=(P_F)_{su}\), and
\[
 h=P_{ii}+Q_{tt}-P_{ii}Q_{tt}.
\]
Then \([D\mathcal P_r(M^{it})[E_{it}]]_{it}=h\), and consequently
\[
 \delta=\frac{[P_Xe+eP_F-P_XeP_F]_{it}}{1-h}.
\]

The required division is legitimate.  With \(X_C=(x_j^{\top})_{j\in C(t)}\), Sherman--Morrison and the positive-definite donor Gram give
\[
 P_{ii}=\frac{x_i^{\top}A_t^{-1}x_i}{1+x_i^{\top}A_t^{-1}x_i}<1,
 \qquad
 \frac{P_{ij}}{1-P_{ii}}=x_i^{\top}A_t^{-1}x_j=a_{ij,t}.
\]
Likewise the positive-definite pretreatment Gram gives
\[
 Q_{tt}=\frac{f_t^{\top}B_S^{-1}f_t}{1+f_t^{\top}B_S^{-1}f_t}<1,
 \qquad
 \frac{Q_{st}}{1-Q_{tt}}=f_s^{\top}B_S^{-1}f_t=b_{t,s}.
\]
Thus \(1-h=(1-P_{ii})(1-Q_{tt})>0\).  Since \(e_{it}=0\), expansion of the numerator retains all three observed blocks:
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 [P_Xe+eP_F-P_XeP_F]_{it}
 &=(1-Q_{tt})\sum_{j\in C(t)}P_{ij}e_{jt}
 +(1-P_{ii})\sum_{s\in S}Q_{st}e_{is}\\
 &\quad-\sum_{j\in C(t)}\sum_{s\in S}P_{ij}Q_{st}e_{js}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Dividing by \((1-P_{ii})(1-Q_{tt})\) therefore yields
\[
 \delta
 =\sum_{j\in C(t)}a_{ij,t}e_{jt}
 +\sum_{s\in S}b_{t,s}e_{is}
 -\sum_{j\in C(t)}\sum_{s\in S}a_{ij,t}b_{t,s}e_{js}
 =\ell_{it}(e).
\]
The donor and pretreatment Gram lower bounds hold uniformly over targets, so every inverse and every denominator used above is uniformly valid.  The donor-pre overlap is therefore part of the differential, not a remainder.

Fix \((i,t)\in G\times W\) and put \(\mathcal H_{it}=\sigma(\epsilon_{js}:j\ne i,\ s\in J)\vee\sigma(\epsilon_{is}:|s-t|>q)\).  By Definition \(\mathrm{def:neighbor\mbox{-}replaced\mbox{-}auxiliary}\), every entry of the auxiliary input
\[
 M^{it}+P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}(\epsilon^{(-it)})
\]
is measurable with respect to \(\mathcal H_{it}\vee\sigma(M,\Omega)=\mathcal G_{it}^{(-t)}\).  The mask is nonrandom by \(\mathrm{ass:deterministic\mbox{-}mask}\), and the optimizer selection, restriction, coordinate projections, and rank projection are fixed measurable maps.  Their composition, and hence \(\widehat M^{\mathrm{aux}}_{it}\), is \(\mathcal G_{it}^{(-t)}\)-measurable.

It remains to prove the asserted separation.  Conditional on \(M\), \(\mathrm{ass:independent\mbox{-}rows}\) makes the full row sigma-field of row \(i\) independent of the joined sigma-field of all rows \(j\ne i\).  Within row \(i\), apply \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\mbox{-}block\mbox{-}dependence}\) with \(\mathcal A=\{t\}\) and \(\mathcal B=\{s\in J:|s-t|>q\}\).  Their distance is greater than \(q\), so
\[
 \sigma(\epsilon_{it})\perp\!\!\!\perp
 \sigma(\epsilon_{is}:|s-t|>q)\mid M.
\]
Combining this within-row factorization with the conditional product law across rows gives
\[
 \sigma(\epsilon_{it})\perp\!\!\!\perp\mathcal H_{it}\mid M.
\]
Because \(\Omega\) is deterministic, adjoining it to the conditioning sigma-field does not change this factorization.  Consequently
\[
 \epsilon_{it}\perp\!\!\!\perp\mathcal G_{it}^{(-t)}\mid(M,\Omega).
\]
Only the singleton target coordinate is separated; no independence of the whole deleted neighborhood has been used.

Write \(u_i=D^{-1/2}x_i\) and \(v_t=D^{-1/2}f_t\), with column-vector conventions.  Incoherence and balanced growth give, uniformly in their indices,
\[
 \lVert u_i\rVert_2\le Cn^{-1/2},
 \qquad \lVert v_t\rVert_2\le Cn^{-1/2}.
\]
Moreover the two normalized Gram assumptions say
\[
 \sum_{j\in C(t)}u_ju_j^{\top}\succeq c_AI_r,
 \qquad \sum_{s\in S}v_sv_s^{\top}\succeq c_BI_r.
\]
Hence Cauchy--Schwarz and the inverse bounds imply
\[
 |a_{ij,t}|
 =\left|u_i^{\top}\left(\sum_{k\in C(t)}u_ku_k^{\top}\right)^{-1}u_j\right|
 \le \frac{C}{n},
 \qquad
 |b_{t,s}|
 =\left|v_t^{\top}\left(\sum_{u\in S}v_uv_u^{\top}\right)^{-1}v_s\right|
 \le \frac{C}{n}.
\]
Under the common-start mask the donor set is \(C(t)=I\setminus G\).  Expanding the complete score inside Definition \(\mathrm{def:oracle\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}variance}\), its three disjoint supports have weights
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 w_{jt}^{(1)}&=\frac{1}{gH}\sum_{i\in G}a_{ij,t},&&j\in C(t),\ t\in W,\\
 w_{is}^{(2)}&=\frac{1}{gH}\sum_{t\in W}b_{t,s},&&i\in G,\ s\in S,\\
 w_{js}^{(3)}&=-\frac{1}{gH}\sum_{i\in G}\sum_{t\in W}a_{ij,t}b_{t,s},&&j\in I\setminus G,\ s\in S.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Therefore
\[
 \max|w^{(1)}|\le\frac{C}{nH},
 \qquad \max|w^{(2)}|\le\frac{C}{gn},
 \qquad \max|w^{(3)}|\le\frac{C}{n^2}.
\]
The cohort-fraction assumption gives \(g\asymp n\).  The donor-window, treated-pre, and donor-pre supports have respectively at most \(CnH\), \(Cgn\), and \(Cn^2\) coordinates.  Since they are disjoint,
\[
 \sum_{j\in I}\sum_{s'\in J}w_{js'}^2
 \le C\left\{\frac{1}{nH}+\frac{1}{gn}+\frac{1}{n^2}\right\}
 \le \frac{C}{nH}.
\]
Variance nondegeneracy supplies \(s^2\ge c_s/(nH)\), and thus
\[
 s^{-2}\sum_{j,s'}w_{js'}^2\le C.
\]
It also gives \(s\ge c(nH)^{-1/2}\).  Since \(1\le H\le Cn\),
\[
 \frac{\max_{j,s'}|w_{js'}|}{s}
 \le C\left\{\frac{1}{\sqrt{nH}}+\frac{\sqrt{nH}}{n^2}\right\}
 \le C\left(n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}\right)\longrightarrow0.
\]
All constants depend only on the fixed incoherence, Gram, rank, aspect-ratio, and variance bounds, proving both assertions uniformly over \(\mathcal P_n\).

The normalized-factor argument in the proof of \(\mathrm{lem:score\mbox{-}diffuseness}\) uses only balanced growth, incoherence, and the two restricted-Gram bounds.  It therefore gives uniformly on every compact exponent set
\[
 |a_{ij,t}|\le Cn^{-1},
 \qquad |b_{t,s}|\le Cn^{-1}.
\]
With \(g\asymp n^b\) and \(H\asymp n^c\), expansion of the three-term score gives
\[
 \max_{j,s'}|w_{js'}|
 \le C\max\left\{\frac1{nH},\frac1{ng},\frac1{n^2}\right\}
\]
and, by counting the same three disjoint supports,
\[
 \sum_{j,s'}w_{js'}^2
 \le C\left\{\frac1{nH}+\frac1{ng}+\frac1{n^2}\right\}.
\]
The frontier variance lower bound is
\[
 s^2\ge c_v\left\{\frac1{nH}+\frac1{ng}\right\},
\]
so the squared-weight sum divided by \(s^2\) is uniformly bounded.  Each component of the maximum is negligible relative to \(s\):
\[
 \frac{(nH)^{-1}}{s}\le\frac1{\sqrt{nH}},
 \qquad
 \frac{(ng)^{-1}}{s}\le\frac1{\sqrt{ng}},
 \qquad
 \frac{n^{-2}}{s}\le \frac{\sqrt{nH}}{n^2}+\frac{\sqrt{ng}}{n^2}.
\]
On a compact subset of \([1/2,1]\times(0,1]\times[0,1]\), the exponent \(b\) is bounded below by a positive constant, while \(c\ge0\).  Thus \(nH\to\infty\), \(ng\to\infty\), and every right-hand side tends to zero uniformly.  This proves the frontier diffuseness claims.

proposed_assumptions.condition:
Almost surely, the conditional exponential moments satisfy
\[
 \sup_{i\in I,\,t\in J}\mathbb E\!\left[\exp\!\left(\epsilon_{it}^2/K^2\right)\middle|M\right]\le2.
\]
proposed_assumptions.reason: The targets assert conditional, uniform Gaussian approximation, whereas the frozen unconditional Orlicz bound does not control conditional third moments uniformly almost surely.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A uniform second-order expansion of the implemented masked nuclear-norm fixed point, including centered quadratic aggregation, cubic and penalty terms, absolute curvature plug-in stability, pretreatment reconstruction, and relative fitted-weight consistency.
open_obligations.obstruction: The exact proximal identity supplies only a self-consistent nonsmooth map. The frozen assumptions do not yet yield a proved simultaneous active-rank neighborhood, a quantitative contraction for all shared-data local fits, or concentration of the aggregate overlapping quadratic forms. Pointwise projector Taylor expansion does not imply the asserted signed aggregate rates.
open_obligations.attempted: Reduced the optimizer to its exact singular-value-thresholding fixed point, derived the full tangent, conditioned through the neighborhood-replaced fit, and converted each asserted raw rate to the oracle standard-error scale. Nonexpansiveness alone loses the averaging gain and does not control regularization or Hessian plug-in error.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The proved proximal identity reduces every local convex fit to the actual self-consistent map
\[
 A\longmapsto\operatorname{SVT}_{\lambda}\!\left(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}+P_{(\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it})^c}A\right),
\]
the complete first differential is the declared three-term score, and the auxiliary fit has the required target-coordinate conditional separation.  If the raw bounds asserted in the target theorem are established, their oracle-scale implication is already deterministic.  Indeed \(s\ge c(nH)^{-1/2}\) and \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge c_{\mathrm{loc}}\psi\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \frac{|Q-B_2|}{s}&=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(\frac{\ell_n^4\sqrt H}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}}\right),\\
 \frac{|R_{\mathrm{agg}}|}{s}
 & =O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(\frac{\ell_n^4n\sqrt H}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}+\frac{\ell_n^4\sqrt H}{n}\right),\\
 \frac{|\widehat B_2-B_2|}{s}
 & =O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(\frac{\ell_n^4n\sqrt H}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2}+\frac{\Delta_\gamma\sqrt{nH}}{\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}}\right).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Under \(\psi\ge n^{1/2+\eta}H^{1/4}\ell_n^8\), the first three displayed deterministic factors are respectively at most constant multiples of
\[
 n^{-1/2-\eta}H^{1/4}\ell_n^{-4},
 \qquad n^{-2\eta}\ell_n^{-12},
 \qquad \ell_n^4\sqrt H/n,
\]
and hence vanish because \(H\le Cn\).  Moreover the asserted reconstruction rate and \(m\asymp n\) would give \(\Delta_\gamma=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^2n^{-1/2})\), making the covariance term vanish as well.  What remains unproved is precisely the native-optimizer source of those raw bounds and the relative fitted-weight bound.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The final claim that the fitted correction makes the native-optimizer aggregate remainder vanish after multiplication by the panel scale.
open_obligations.obstruction: The local singular-value and oracle Hessian-covariance contractions are explicit, but transferring them through the penalized masked fixed point at the inverse-panel scale is exactly the unresolved native second-order problem.
open_obligations.attempted: Computed the local signal normalization, the moving-average covariance, the rank-one projection quadratic map, the parity-specific limits, and their window average. The proximal identity does not by itself bound the corrected native remainder.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The algebraic part of the calibration is exact.  There are \(3n/4+1\) local rows, and the alternating sequence has average squared numerator \(5/4\).  Consequently
\[
 \lVert u^{\mathrm{cal}}_{I_{it}}\rVert_2^2=\frac34+\frac1n,
 \qquad
 \lVert v^{\mathrm{cal}}_{J_{it}}\rVert_2^2=\frac12+\frac{4p_t^2}{5n},
\]
and the rank-one product formula gives
\[
 \frac{\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}}{\psi}
 =\sqrt{\left(\frac34+\frac1n\right)\left(\frac12+\frac{4p_t^2}{5n}\right)}
 \longrightarrow\sqrt{\frac38}>\frac12.
\]
Also \(\epsilon_{it}=z_{it}+z_{i,t-1}/2\) gives \(\gamma(0)=5/4\), \(\gamma(1)=1/2\), and zero covariance beyond lag one.  To contract the curvature, write the normalized local signal as \(\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}uv^{\top}\), and for a perturbation \(E\) put
\[
 c_E=(I-uu^{\top})Ev,
 \quad b_E=(I-vv^{\top})E^{\top}u,
 \quad \mathscr D_E=(I-uu^{\top})E(I-vv^{\top}).
\]
The rank-one projection expansion gives the homogeneous quadratic term
\[
 Q_{it}(E)=\frac{\mathscr D_Eb_Ev^{\top}+u c_E^{\top}\mathscr D_E+c_Eb_E^{\top}}{\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}}.
\]
Substitution of \(E=P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon+\ell_{it}(R_{it}\epsilon)E^{it}_{it}\), followed by contraction of same-row pairs at lags zero and one, yields
\[
 \psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}\,
 \mathbb E\!\left[q_{it}(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon)\mid M\right]
 =-\frac{6\sqrt{3/2}}{5\sqrt5}\,p_t+O(n^{-1}).
\]
Dividing by \(\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}/\psi\to\sqrt{3/8}\) gives
\[
 \psi\,\mathbb E[q_{it}(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon)\mid M]
 \longrightarrow-\frac{12p_t}{5\sqrt5}=\kappa_t^{\mathrm{drift}}.
\]
The window length \(n/4\) is even along \(n\in8\mathbb N\), so the window has equally many targets of each parity and \(\psi B_2\to-12/(5\sqrt5)\).  This verifies the signal and oracle-curvature portions of the proposition; it does not establish the asserted \(n\)-scaled remainder for the fitted native optimizer.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The conditional uniform Lyapunov bound under the frozen moment assumptions.
open_obligations.obstruction: An unconditional sub-Gaussian norm bound permits conditional third moments given the signal to be arbitrarily large on rare signal events, so it does not establish the almost-sure conditional uniform approximation stated in the target.
open_obligations.attempted: Derived coordinate diffuseness and reduced the bounded-degree dependency-graph error to a conditional third-moment sum. Proposed the standard conditional sub-Gaussian strengthening rather than assuming the Gaussian limit.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The proved score-diffuseness bounds reduce the conditional central limit theorem to conditional moment control.  Under the proposed conditional sub-Gaussian assumption, the variables \(X_{js}=w_{js}\epsilon_{js}/s\), conditional on \((M,\Omega)\), have a dependency graph of maximum degree at most \(2q\), satisfy
\[
 \sum_{j,s}\mathbb E(|X_{js}|^3\mid M,\Omega)
 \le C_qK^3\frac{\max_{j,s}|w_{js}|}{s}\frac{\sum_{j,s}w_{js}^2}{s^2}=o(1),
\]
and have total conditional variance one by the definition of \(s^2\).  The usual characteristic-function proof for bounded-degree dependency graphs then yields the stated uniform Gaussian limit.  The existing unconditional Orlicz bound alone does not make the displayed conditional Lyapunov quantity uniformly bounded almost surely.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The compact-uniform conditional Lyapunov bound over the exponent-indexed classes.
open_obligations.obstruction: Frontier diffuseness is proved, but the same mismatch between unconditional and conditional tail control remains uniformly over the class.
open_obligations.attempted: Substituted the frontier weight bounds into the degree-bounded dependency-graph Lyapunov quantity and isolated the sole missing conditional moment premise.
open_obligations.partial_result:
On every compact exponent subset, frontier score diffuseness gives
\[
 \sup\frac{\sum_{j,s}w_{js}^2}{s^2}<\infty,
 \qquad
 \sup\frac{\max_{j,s}|w_{js}|}{s}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Under the proposed conditional sub-Gaussian assumption, the same degree-\(2q\) dependency-graph calculation gives
\[
 \sup\sum_{j,s}\mathbb E\!\left(\left|\frac{w_{js}\epsilon_{js}}s\right|^3\middle|M,\Omega\right)
 \le C_qK^3\sup\frac{\max|w|}{s}\sup\frac{\sum w^2}{s^2}\longrightarrow0,
\]
which is the compact-uniform Lyapunov reduction.  Conditional tail control is absent from the frozen primitives, so the target cannot yet be marked proved.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The native expansion, feasible curvature and influence-weight plug-in rates, and conditional score limit needed for studentization and uniform coverage.
open_obligations.obstruction: Causal cancellation and variance-consistency algebra are exact, but the frozen core does not prove the native second-order theorem, and its unconditional tail condition is insufficient for the stated conditional uniform central limit theorem.
open_obligations.attempted: Derived the exact causal error identity, decomposed the corrected estimator, and proved a Toeplitz-operator bound reducing variance consistency to covariance and weight consistency. The remaining inputs coincide with the separately isolated obligations.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The causal algebra is exact.  By consistency and the common-start mask, \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{it}=Y_{it}(1)\) on \(G\times W\); hence the definitions of \(\tau\) and \(\widehat\tau\) give
\[
 \widehat\tau-\tau
 =-\frac1{gH}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it}).
\]
If the native expansion holds, then
\[
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau
 =-L-(Q-B_2)-R_{\mathrm{agg}}+(\widehat B_2-B_2).
\]
Thus the remainder statements in the native-transfer theorem imply \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau=-L+o_{\mathbb P}(s)\).

There is also an exact variance-consistency reduction.  Let \(d=\widehat w-w\) and let \(\Gamma_q\) and \(\widehat\Gamma_q\) be the banded Toeplitz matrices generated by \(\gamma\) and \(\widehat\gamma\).  Fixed \(q\), sub-Gaussian second moments, and \(\Delta_\gamma=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) imply bounded operator norms, and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\widehat V-s^2|
 &\le \lVert\widehat\Gamma_q\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \left(2\lVert w\rVert_F\lVert d\rVert_F+\lVert d\rVert_F^2\right)
 +\lVert\widehat\Gamma_q-\Gamma_q\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\lVert w\rVert_F^2\\
 &\le C_q\left\{\lVert w\rVert_F\lVert d\rVert_F+\lVert d\rVert_F^2+\Delta_\gamma\lVert w\rVert_F^2\right\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Score diffuseness gives \(\lVert w\rVert_F^2=O(s^2)\), so \(\lVert d\rVert_F^2=o_{\mathbb P}(s^2)\) yields \(\widehat V/s^2\to_{\mathbb P}1\).  Conditional Slutsky and the conditional score limit would then prove the displayed studentized limit and Wald coverage.  The two missing premises are the native optimizer and plug-in rates and, for the conditional limit as written, the proposed conditional tail assumption.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A source-verified equality with the exact Choi--Yuan one-date theorem and a native curvature estimate proving that the drift is negligible relative to the standard error.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen core contains neither a cited leaf transcribing the published theorem nor a proved native curvature rate. The publication comparison therefore cannot be established solely by the current mathematical primitives.
open_obligations.attempted: Specialized the full tangent score to zero dependence and one target date and proved that its donor-pre overlap component is negligible at the target standard-error scale.
open_obligations.partial_result:
At \(q=0\) and \(H=1\), the complete score remains
\[
 \ell_{it}(e)=\sum_{j\in C(t)}a_{ij,t}e_{jt}
 +\sum_{s\in S}b_{t,s}e_{is}
 -\sum_{j\in C(t),s\in S}a_{ij,t}b_{t,s}e_{js}.
\]
The weight calculation above shows that the donor-pre overlap component has squared weight norm \(O(n^{-2})\), whereas variance nondegeneracy gives \(s^2\asymp n^{-1}\); hence that component is \(o_{\mathbb P}(s)\).  Establishing the claimed exact reduction additionally requires a source-verified statement of Choi--Yuan's theorem and a proved native curvature bound implying \(B_2=o(s)\).  Neither premise is present as an established node in the frozen core.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The raw cohort-dependent native-optimizer bounds, their complete finite system of affine exponent inequalities, and matching exterior Gaussian witnesses for every face.
open_obligations.obstruction: The only displayed native rates belong to the proportional-cohort theorem and remain unproved there. They contain no derived dependence on a sparse growing cohort, and no primitive argument supplies the requested necessity witnesses; declaring their conditional substitution to be sharp would assume the crux.
open_obligations.attempted: Proved frontier score diffuseness and the conditional score-CLT reduction, then substituted the conjectured proportional-cohort rates into the declared oracle scale to expose the inequalities they would generate. This does not certify sharpness or transfer those rates to the frontier class.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Let \(d=\min\{b,c\}\), so the declared frontier variance has \(s\asymp n^{-(1+d)/2}\).  If the bounded-aspect raw rates displayed in the native-transfer target extended uniformly to the frontier class, exponent substitution would give
\[
 \frac{\ell_n^4}{\psi\sqrt n\,s}=\ell_n^4n^{d/2-a},
 \qquad
 \frac{\ell_n^4\sqrt n}{\psi^2s}=\ell_n^4n^{1+d/2-2a},
 \qquad
 \frac{\ell_n^4n^{-3/2}}s=\ell_n^4n^{-1+d/2}.
\]
With \(m\asymp n\) and the asserted reconstruction rate, the covariance plug-in term has the first of these polynomial exponents up to logarithms.  Thus those conjectured rates would at least require the affine inequalities
\[
 a>\frac d2,
 \qquad 2a>1+\frac d2,
 \qquad d<2,
\]
of which the middle inequality is the binding one on the declared exponent box.  This is only a conditional reduction: the frozen core supplies neither the \(g\)-dependent native-transfer, Hessian, and weight-plug-in rates nor exterior Gaussian witnesses.  It therefore does not determine a sharp region \(\mathfrak F\).
